paper_title: Cosmological bounds on pseudo Nambu-Goldstone bosons
coupling_convention: Log10 of ALP lifetime tau in seconds (NOT a coupling). The y-axis of Fig. 6 is Log10 tau [s]; emitted values are these lifetimes as plotted.
notes: Theory/review paper establishing cosmological bounds on ALPs with two-photon coupling g (GeV^-1) vs mass m_phi (eV), from BBN (D, 4He), N_eff (WMAP7), CMB spectral distortions, EBL/optical/X-ray/gamma-ray decay searches, and DM overclosure. Main results are the exclusion regions in Figs. 1 and 2 (mphi-g and mphi-tau planes), which are a complex patchwork of regions with characteristic slope g ∝ m^-3/2, not a single tabulated curve. No numerical table is provided, so precise (mass, coupling) pairs cannot be reliably extracted from text. The only analytic boundary given is the low-mass validity edge of the N_eff bound: g/GeV^-1 ≳ 10^-3 (eV/m_phi)^3/2 (Eq. 3.11). Coupling type is clearly AxionPhoton; data extraction quality is low because values live only in figures. | [VISION GATE D] vision notes admit tracing a compilation envelope ('union of') rather than the paper's own single curve | selector: figure_vision (sole candidate) | Vision: The flagged exclusion plot (Fig. 6) is a lifetime (Log10 tau [s]) vs mass (Log10 m_phi [MeV]) plot showing BBN constraints (deuterium underproduction D, helium overproduction 4He, photodissociation gamma-He/gamma-D, hadronic cascades, neutrino dilution Neff). It is NOT a g_agamma-vs-mass coupling plot; the paper's g_agamma exclusion curves are Figs. 1 and 2 (not among the images flagged as the exclusion plot). Because tau = 64*pi/(m^3 g^2), the plotted y-quantity is inversely related to g^2, so a naive treatment as a coupling is invalid. I traced the LOWER boundary of the union of the colored excluded regions: flat at Log10 tau ~ -4 (bottom) for masses up to ~10^5.3 eV (0.2 MeV), rising through the white unexcluded notch near m_phi ~ 1 MeV (peak Log10 tau ~ 1.2), then settling to ~ -1.5 at high mass. Values emitted are Log10 tau [s], not couplings. Extraction confidence is deliberately very low because the y-axis is a lifetime, not any coupling constant. | Calibration: No calibration needed (spot-check verify/stage2 raw_ratio=1.67 snapped to identity) | contract: median outside VALID_RANGES after corrections (flagged low confidence)
